title: Inquest called into death of man passed out in jail
article: An inquest will be held into a man who died after being in Ridge Meadows RCMP custody in October 2008.

Fifty-four-year-old Ian Alexander Young was found unresponsive while in a Maple Ridge jail cell early in the morning on October 18. He died after undergoing surgery at Royal Columbian Hospital. The man was taken into custody on October 17 after BC Ambulance Service received a call around 10 p.m. about a man found lying on the side of the road in an intoxicated state. The RCMP's Integrated Homicide Investigation Team's (IHIT) spokesperson Cpl. Dale Carr said BC Ambulance employees did an assessment and determined he didn't need to be taken to the hospital.

Carr said the man was "intoxicated to the point where he couldn't care for himself" so he was arrested and taken into RCMP cells. Several hours later, at 6:30 a.m. he was found to be unresponsive but still breathing. BC Ambulance Service was called and took him to Ridge Meadows Hospital. From there he was transported to Royal Columbian Hospital. Carr said the surgery was for a pre-existing injury that occurred prior to being arrested by police.
Young's inquest is scheduled for August 10 to 13 in Burnaby.

A jury will hear evidence from subpoenaed witnesses in order to determine the facts surrounding his death. The jury can make recommendations on how to prevent similar deaths in the future but can't assign blame.
